name: DR Congo
region: Eastern Congo — North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri
summary: Eastern Congo faces one of the world's longest-running humanitarian crises. Armed groups, including the M23 rebel movement, have displaced over 7 million people amid widespread violence, sexual violence, and a scramble for conflict minerals.
context:
The Democratic Republic of Congo has endured decades of conflict, instability, and exploitation. The eastern provinces of North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri are home to over 100 armed groups vying for control of territory rich in minerals essential to global technology supply chains — coltan, cobalt, tin, and gold.

The M23 rebel group, widely reported to receive support from neighboring Rwanda, has intensified its offensive since late 2022, capturing significant territory and displacing hundreds of thousands. The UN Group of Experts and multiple investigations have documented Rwanda's involvement, which Rwanda denies.

The humanitarian impact is immense. The DRC has the largest number of internally displaced people in Africa and one of the largest in the world. Displacement camps around Goma and other cities are overcrowded, lacking adequate food, water, and sanitation. Outbreaks of cholera, measles, and mpox have compounded the crisis.

Sexual violence has been used as a weapon of war by multiple armed groups, with the DRC consistently ranked among the worst places in the world for gender-based violence in conflict. Survivors face stigma and often lack access to medical and psychological care.

The connection between Congo's minerals and global consumer electronics is a critical but often overlooked dimension. Cobalt mined in artisanal conditions — including by children — powers the batteries in smartphones, laptops, and electric vehicles worldwide. Advocacy for supply chain transparency and conflict-free sourcing is an important avenue for action.

awareness: Learn and share the connection between conflict minerals (cobalt, coltan, tin) and consumer electronics — your phone is linked to this crisis
Follow Congolese journalists and activists on social media to amplify voices from the ground, not just international coverage
Share documentaries and reporting that explain the historical roots of the conflict, including colonial exploitation and resource extraction
Organize teach-ins or campus events about the DRC crisis — it is one of the world's deadliest and least covered conflicts
Demand that tech companies in your life publish transparent supply chain audits for conflict minerals
political: Urge your representatives to support and strengthen the Dodd-Frank Section 1502 conflict minerals provision and its enforcement
Call for sanctions against armed group leaders and foreign officials documented as fueling the conflict in eastern Congo
Advocate for increased U.S. and EU humanitarian funding for the DRC — the UN appeal is consistently among the most underfunded
Support calls for accountability at the International Criminal Court for war crimes and crimes against humanity in the DRC
Push for diplomatic pressure on Rwanda regarding its documented support for M23 rebels
